key_insight: Four ECG foundation models shared age-related performance gaps that appear rooted in ECG data and labels rather than model architecture.
clinical_relevance: Overall performance can mask poorer discrimination in older adults, supporting age-stratified evaluation before clinical deployment.
method: Evaluated four frozen ECG foundation models across 31 endpoints, stratifying performance by age, sex and race.
Compared pretrained models with untrained copies and logistic regression using classical ECG measurements.
Tested post-hoc correction, larger labelled datasets, comorbidity exclusion and low-rank fine-tuning.
evidence_signal: Across 5.4 million ECGs in 13 cohorts, including six held-out cohorts, the median age-related AUROC gap was 0.028 versus 0.004 for sex and 0.016 for race; tested mitigations did not close it.
watch_item: These results support a data-related origin but do not establish a single cause; age-specific thresholds and recalibration still require validation.
paper_title: ECG foundation models share an age-related performance disparity that originates in the data, not the models
